roles: encapsulate multiple network-layer protocols over point-to-point links
provide hooks for authentication and extensions
addressing: Network-layer addressing is configured by appropriate Network Control Protocols rather than being inherent in the generic PPP frame.
error_control: PPP framing detects damaged frames according to the selected framing specification; reliable retransmission of carried network traffic is not the generic PPP core responsibility.

operations.monitoring: Link-state and negotiation phases are visible through LCP/NCP exchanges and implementation logs.
operations.diagnostics: Negotiation failures, authentication failures, framing errors and protocol-reject/code-reject behavior are operationally important.
operations.failure_behavior: Link establishment can fail during physical availability, LCP negotiation, authentication, or NCP configuration.
operations.operator_interface: Dialer scripts, access-server configuration and PPP daemon options are implementation-specific.

survival.provenance_notes: PPP remains present in several descendant access technologies; repository records should distinguish later branches such as PPPoE.

open_questions: Trace PAP/CHAP and IPCP as separate protocol genealogies.
Recover early PPP implementations in Unix, KA9Q, routers and access servers.
Map PPP framing RFC 1549→1662 separately from the PPP core revision chain.

supports: early PPP proposal and Working Group ancestry

related_artifacts.notes: PPP generalizes the serial point-to-point access role beyond SLIP's IP-only minimal framing; not a formal RFC revision of SLIP.

notes: PPP is a negotiated point-to-point link architecture, not merely a more featureful SLIP frame delimiter.
